definitions.gloss: to soothe, to calm down, to pacify
definitions.explanation: To comfort or placate someone who is upset, angry, or crying, using gentle words or actions.

examples.japanese: {泣|な}いている{子|こ}を{宥|なだ}める。
{怒|おこ}っている{妻|つま}を{何|なん}とか{宥|なだ}めた。
examples.english: I somehow managed to calm down my angry wife.

examples.japanese: 「{落|お}ち{着|つ}いて」と{言|い}って、{興奮|こうふん}している{彼|かれ}を{宥|なだ}めようとした。
examples.english: Saying "Calm down," I tried to pacify him as he was worked up.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). Pattern: Xを{宥|なだ}める.

USAGE:
Used when dealing with someone in an emotional state — crying, angry, or panicking. The subject is always trying to restore calm through words, gestures, or comfort.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {子供|こども}を{宥|なだ}める: to soothe a child
- {怒|いか}りを{宥|なだ}める: to calm someone's anger
- {泣|な}いている{人|ひと}を{宥|なだ}める: to comfort someone who is crying

SIMILAR WORDS:
{落|お}ち{着|つ}かせる means "to make someone calm down" and is more neutral. {宥|なだ}める implies a gentler, more soothing approach, often with words of comfort. {慰|なぐさ}める (to console) focuses more on emotional comfort after loss or sadness, whereas {宥|なだ}める focuses on calming active distress.
